messages.author: 237c46255b49e6ef
messages.subject: reverse coding and negative variance
parts:
Hi all,

I am quite new to R and have tried to perform CFA with five personality traits (which I wanted to create as a latent variable) consisting of five manifest variables.

Here are the questions/variables from my survey data :
1. Extraversion  
   - S38.1: ... I am introverted. 
   - S38.6: ... I am outgoing, social.

2. Agreeableness
   - S38.2: ... I generally trust people.
   - S38.7: ... I tend to find faults in others.

3. Conscientiousness 
   - S38.3: ... I tend to be lazy.
   - S38.8: ... I complete my work thoroughly.

4. Emotional Stability
   - S38.4: ... I am relaxed, I cope well with stress.
   - S38.9: ... I get angry easily. 

5. Openness to Experience 
   - S38.5: ... I have very little artistic interest. 
   - S38.10: ... I have an active imagination.

and values for these questions/items are : (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Agree, 5=Strongly agree.)

I tried to make reverse coding for some items : 

affect_data$S38.1 <- 6 - affect_data$S38.1
affect_data$S38.7 <- 6 - affect_data$S38.7
affect_data$S38.3 <- 6 - affect_data$S38.3
affect_data$S38.9 <- 6 - affect_data$S38.9
affect_data$S38.5 <- 6 - affect_data$S38.5

Later I performed CFA :

model_personality <- '
    Extraversion =~ S38.6 + S38.1
    Agreeableness =~ S38.2 + S38.7
    Conscientiousness =~ S38.8 + S38.3
    Emotional_Stability =~ S38.4 + S38.9
    Openness_to_Experience =~ S38.10 + S38.5
'
fit_personality <- cfa(model_personality, data=affect_data)
summary(fit_personality, fit.measures=TRUE)

but I encountered negative variance : 

Variances: Estimate Std.Err z-value P(>|z|) .S38.6 1.059 NA .S38.1 -291.829 NA .S38.2 1.117 NA .S38.7 1.108 NA .S38.8 1.221 NA .S38.3 -318.647 NA .S38.4 1.035 NA .S38.9 1.178 NA .S38.10 0.843 NA .S38.5 0.961 NA Extraversion 0.000 NA Agreeableness 0.120 NA Conscientisnss 0.000 NA Emotinl_Stblty 0.006 NA Opnnss_t_Exprn 0.159 NA

I was wondering whether the problem occurs due to my mistake in reverse coding. Also, how can I convert the negative variance into positive?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 38226bd700051927
messages.subject: Re: reverse coding and negative variance
parts:
Your reverse coding is correct, for what I can tell.

The problem is most likely due to only having two observed variables as indicators of each factor, which makes the model underidentified. Under these circumstances, you need to add additional constraints. A typical one in this case would be to constrain the factor loadings for the two items indicating each factor to be equal.

Hope that helps!

--
Daniel Morillo, Ph.D.
